opportunities.what_to_build: Submitted abstract: REEFPRINT (Category: Problem 3: Computer Vision for Real-Time Mineralogical Characterisation, by Lethabo). Rather than building a mineral classifier that competes with lab instruments (SEM/XRD/QEMSCAN), distills those instruments' existing output as a 'teacher' into a cheap optical model that reproduces their maps in seconds instead of days. Targets five Bushveld-relevant phases: chromite, orthopyroxene, plagioclase, base-metal sulphide, talc/serpentine: deliberately including base-metal sulphide even at <1% by area since that's where PGM economic value sits; the abstract commits to reporting per-class recall on that sub-1% class ahead of any aggregate accuracy number. Converts texture/liberation into three metallurgical response variables (liberation, reagent demand, grindability) feeding a plant setpoint recommendation with calibrated uncertainty: abstains rather than guessing when confidence is low. Frames cost/impact in Rand and tCO2e using real SA gazetted rates (Eskom Megaflex, carbon tax). Positioned as a module for Mintek's existing StarCS/FloatStar/MillStar platform, not a competing product. Code has since been re-scoped to match the submitted phase set.

opportunities.team_fit: SUBMITTED 18 Aug 2026, 13 days ahead of the 31 Aug Phase 1 close — the same "submit early" discipline Standing Agreement 6 asks for on every other entry, applied here on its own initiative. This is the only entry on the board that is genuinely NOT a shared team submission: SME Toolkit's eligibility is individual, so Sibusiso and Lethabo each entered their own separate business (see what_to_build). Practically, that means Phase 1 workshops, Phase 2 finalist interviews and any award are tracked per person, not per team — one plan could advance without the other. opportunities.what_to_build:
TWO separate individual business plans were submitted for Phase 1, one per team member — SME Toolkit's eligibility is individual ("young and aspiring business owners"), not team-based, so this is the one entry on the board where the two of you compete as separate entrants rather than one shared submission.

PLAN 1 (Sibusiso) — Karoo Compute: shared GPU/AI compute infrastructure for South Africa. Problem: no modern data-centre GPU is rentable inside SA — AWS Cape Town tops out at the 2020-era T4, GCP Johannesburg lists none at all, and the CHPC's 30 V100s (2018) were compromised for cryptomining in June 2026, causing weeks of downtime; UNDP puts 95% of Africa's AI talent on GPU-less laptops. Business: buy data-centre GPUs, colocate Tier III in Johannesburg, rent hourly/monthly/yearly in rand across five products — Karoo Campus (R9.50/GPU-hr, subsidised idle capacity for students/academics), Karoo Build (R21.50/hr or R11,900/mo reserved, for startups/corporates), Karoo Studio (96GB high-memory, Year 2), Karoo Inference (token-priced endpoints), Karoo Deploy (dedicated cluster builds for institutions). Why now: 440+ consecutive days without load-shedding, Eskom courting buyers for ~6GW surplus; Megaflex power at ~R1.65/kWh (~10c) vs 15–20c across Europe is worth R6,600–R13,200 more margin per GPU per year than an identical offshore operator gets; 0% GPU import duty, VAT recoverable. HostAfrica's March 2026 Johannesburg GPU launch (40–95% premium over international rates) already proved local willingness to pay — Karoo prices 33–41% below that and still holds 63% gross margin at scale. Plan: R1.75m Year 1 (founders' equity + NYDA grant + dtic SPII + SEDFA loan), one 4-GPU node plus one institutional cluster build, prove utilisation above the 46% break-even before deploying real capital. Revenue R865k (Yr1) → R29.3m (Yr5); EBITDA-positive Yr3, profitable after tax Yr5; 12 employees; ~380,000 subsidised GPU-hours to SA students/researchers over five years. Full 48-page plan and live 5-year financial model (income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, monthly Yr1 cash flow, unit economics, 4 scenarios) already built, to be refined at the workshop.

PLAN 2 (Lethabo) — Indlela AI: an AI engineering studio building agentic AI, data science and data engineering systems for SA companies ("indlela" = the path — pilot to production to governed system). Problem: 67% of large SA enterprises have adopted GenAI, but only 14% have a formal strategy and 13% a governance framework; 39% cite implementation cost as their biggest obstacle; four recurring causes — unfit data, no evaluation harness, no post-launch ownership, ungovernable systems. POPIA section 71 already bans solely-automated decisions with legal/substantial effect absent human review and explainability — binding on every automated credit/underwriting/fraud decision in SA today, met by almost nothing deployed. Opportunity: 35% of African companies already use agentic AI, 44% plan to soon; multi-agent orchestration is SA's fastest-growing AI segment at 29.3% CAGR; a May 2026 "top 7 AI-agent development companies" listicle named zero South African firms. Three engines: (1) Studio — fixed-scope, fixed-price 3-week Proof-of-Value sprint from R185,000 ending in a written go/no-go; ~45% convert to a production build then a managed-ops retainer, so client acquisition is itself a paid, profitable engagement; (2) Products — a pattern register hardened into licensed products after the third repeat build: Agent Foundry (governance/evaluation control plane with POPIA s71 review and explainability workflows) and Indlela Docs (SA-specific document processing — FICA packs, payslips, municipal accounts, medical claims); (3) Academy — ICT roles went from 10% to 22% of SA's hardest-to-fill positions in three years and 84% of large corporates can't source skilled talent, against 12.2% graduate unemployment (22.2% for other tertiary qualifications); 12-month cohorts funded by corporate Skills Development budgets, cash-positive per learner in Year 1, each graduate generating ~5.5x their training cost in first-year billing. Why us: 100% black-owned Exempted Micro Enterprise, Level 1 B-BBEE by affidavit — every rand a corporate spends is recognised at R1.35 on their own scorecard, so pricing at parity is materially cheaper to the buyer. Numbers: R950k Year 1 funding (mostly working capital for 50-day enterprise debtors), profitable and cash-generative from Year 1; revenue R3.08m → R65.1m by Year 5 at a 22.6% EBITDA margin; no external equity raised post-incorporation; all interest-bearing debt repaid by Year 5; 63 employees including academy learners. Full 49-page plan and live 5-year financial model already built, to be refined at the workshop.
